thread:
jess (support): AcmeApp reported a regression after last night's rollout — same prompt returns old onboarding copy. Customer pasted request_id=req_0x9f3a and a quick repro. Can we triage? :thinking_face:
AcmeApp (customer): Example: prompt `\"Hi, show onboarding message\"` -> got `Welcome to Acme v1 - legacy onboarding` but expected `Welcome to Acme v2 - new flow`. Happening for ~30% of calls. Route: /v1/generate, model=redwood-instruct-2, region=us-west-2. Headers: `x-request-id=req_0x9f3a` `x-kv-prefix: acme_user_42:v1` `x-cache-hit: true`
jess (support): Repro steps the customer provided:```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-instruct-2","input":"Hi, show onboarding message","request_id":"req_0x9f3a"}'
```
luis (eng-runtime): Can you paste the full response headers and the `x-deploy-tag`? Also did the customer hit a canary node or full rollout? :eyes:
AcmeApp (customer): Headers we captured: `x-request-id:req_0x9f3a`, `x-deploy-tag:dpl-579`, `x-kv-prefix:acme_user_42:v1`, `x-cache-hit:true`, `x-node-id:usw2-n-14`. We did one request to canary and several to prod.
anya (eng-ml): Sounds like a namespace/versioning mismatch in KV prefixing. We recently shipped a change that tweaks prefix generation (adds account hash + opt-in version token). If some nodes used the old prefix (v1) and others use the new logic (v2), cached responses keyed under the old namespace will still be valid and served -> stale template. This matches `x-kv-prefix: acme_user_42:v1` being returned.
sam (eng-runtime): Confirmed. dpl-579 was the canary that introduced the updated prefixing logic. We didn't bump the namespace token because we tried to be backward-compatible. Unfortunately that means old keys remain in caches on some nodes and can be served when routing lands on them.
deploy-bot: deploy dpl-579 completed to canary (2026-03-16T03:21:12Z) :white_check_mark:
luis (eng-runtime): Plan: 1) Evict legacy namespace keys for AcmeUser 42 from KV on affected clusters. 2) Monitor error-rate and sample outputs. 3) If hit-rate persists, roll back dpl-579 from prod and roll forward with prefix bump. I'll run step 1 now and post the commands.
sam (eng-runtime): Eviction command (internal):```bash
curl -X POST https://internal.redwood/v1/kv/evict \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"namespace":"acme_user_42","prefix_version":"v1","regions":["us-west-2"]}'
```  -- requires run on control plane in us-west-2. Use `--dry-run` first if you want to preview.
luis (eng-runtime): Evict started against usw2 cluster, targeting node shard set n-10..n-18. Monitoring logs for `evict:acme_user_42` entries.
jess (support): Asked customer to retry in ~10m after eviction.
AcmeApp (customer): Tried again after 12m — now responses show `Welcome to Acme v2 - new flow`. Looks fixed from our side. Thanks. :raised_hands:
anya (eng-ml): Short-term mitigation: when changing prefix logic we should bump a namespace token (minor version) so old keys cannot be served accidentally. Also add a rollout check that verifies sampling across node shards to catch mixed-prefix serving.
sam (eng-runtime): Agreed. Action items: - add automated eviction hook to canary->prod promotion when prefix algo changes; - add e2e test that exercises cache-key namespace changes across 10k sampled requests; - run a post-mortem if any other customers impacted.
luis (eng-runtime): I'll open a PR with the eviction hook + docs. Jess, can you keep the ticket open till the PR lands and customer confirms 24h stability?
jess (support): Yep — leaving open. Noting customer happy now. Final notes: request_id=req_0x9f3a, affected region=us-west-2, deploy=dpl-579, root cause=mixed KV namespace due to prefix change without namespace bump.
AcmeApp (customer): Appreciate the fast help. Please keep us posted on permanent fix.
— end of thread —
